items.title: Marshall Lawrence Interview, 1960-06-28
items.q: Dajon, Alexander. And at that time the band was named by him, Alexander Right Time Band.

ctx.x: No one. Like I said, the other night, a bunch of boys got together and started a little band, organized a little band, and we bought some instruments, and I had an instrument. Like I said, the first day I had my instrument, I could play in tune. From that we began to take lessons from Mr. John Robichaud. He came out here for about six months. Then he discontinued. We had to get somebody else, which we got Mr. Professor Cleven Williams. He stayed about six months with us. Then from that we began to play little…

Dajon, Alexander. And at that time the band was named by him, Alexander Right Time Band. And after he got droned, then the way Cromont player and myself, we called it Lawrence and Dewey Arbster. So we played, well I don't remember how many years we played together. And he left the country, so we had another boy to play in his place. And we keep switching off, get some new mans until, then we, until this boy came in with us, Herbert Hall. Well he played the banjo and then after he switched to clarinet. And then we…
